page: Amazon Web Services g4ad.4xlarge is a graphics-focused instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor and an AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 600 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. It is designed for graphics-intensive workloads, remote workstations, and game streaming that benefit from AMD GPU acceleration.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance characteristics. The AMD EPYC 7R32 CPU delivers average multi-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. However, single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 10% in stress-ng single-core tests. Memory performance also presents tradeoffs; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

The inclusion of a dedicated AMD GPU with 8 GB of VRAM and 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance highly suitable for graphics rendering, video transcoding, and virtual desktop infrastructure. It also supports moderate machine learning tasks, achieving average text generation speeds on 7B parameter models, though prompt processing speeds remain weak. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g4ad.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for GPU-accelerated tasks that do not require high-end enterprise AI accelerators, providing a cost-effective alternative for mainstream graphics and media processing.
description: Amazon Web Services g4ad.4xlarge is a graphics-optimized instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor with 16 vCPUs, 64 GB of DDR4 memory, and a dedicated AMD Radeon Pro Navi V520 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it includes 600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core CPU and cached memory bandwidth capabilities, though single-core performance and uncached large-block memory bandwidth are relatively weak. The instance is well-suited for graphics-intensive applications, virtual workstations, game streaming, and moderate media processing workloads that benefit from AMD GPU acceleration and local high-speed storage.
